title: AlphaEvolve Scaled Across 67 Open Math Problems Improves Bounds & Generalizes Formulas
whyItMatters: Demonstrated across 67 open problems in analysis, combinatorics, and geometry—co-authored with Terence Tao—that evolutionary LLM agents can systematically beat human bounds at scale.
summary: Bogdan Georgiev, Javier Gómez-Serrano, Terence Tao, and Adam Zsolt Wagner benchmarked Google DeepMind’s AlphaEvolve on 67 open mathematical optimization and construction problems. AlphaEvolve matched best-known human constructions in the majority of cases, discovered strictly improved bounds across multiple open problems (including kissing numbers and Nikodym/overlap constructions), and in several cases generalized finite constructions into symbolic formulas valid for all inputs.
technicalHighlights: Systematically evaluated autonomous evolutionary code search across 67 open problems spanning analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and number theory.
Improved multiple long-standing human bounds and synthesized general closed-form constructions validated by AlphaProof and Deep Think.
Published in PNAS (2026), establishing a scalable methodology for mathematician-AI collaboration.
caveats: Strongest on extremal and constructive problems with fast programmatic scoring functions; conceptual structural proofs still required coupling with separate proof systems.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that automated evolutionary search generalizes across dozens of distinct branches of research mathematics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Provided the operational blueprint for coupling evolutionary search with formal provers across academia.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in PNAS with explicit, programmatically verified constructions and proofs.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed months of bespoke heuristic search across 67 open problems into parallelized agent runs.
